subject: Opsly dedicated renewal — hot-standby topology & scale proposal
messages:
From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Claire Brooks <claire@opsly.ai>, Procurement <procurement@opsly.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Opsly dedicated renewal — hot-standby topology & scale proposal

Claire — thanks for sending ahead the renewal reminder. We ran the usage telemetry you shared through our capacity planner and sketched three pragmatic options that keep your 99th-percentile latency target while giving headroom for a planned model migration later this year.

Short summary of where we landed:
- Current steady-state: ~420 steady H100-equivalent concurrent slots (peak bursts to ~620 for hourly spikes).
- Observed median sequence length: 275 tokens (QPS distribution skewed to daytime batch windows).
- Key ask from you: avoid any runtime interruptions during migration and keep P99 < 450ms for small-text generation workloads.

I attached a compact topology proposal (redwood-proposed-topology-opsly.pdf) and a request for your final usage slice (opsly_usage_q1q2_2028.csv) — can you confirm the attachment we received from you matches these numbers or share the corrected export if not?

Recommended option (brief):
- Hybrid mix: 360 H100-equivalent dedicated slots + 160 A100 burst pool + 100-slot hot-standby across a second availability zone.
- Hot-standby behavior: warm kernels + prefix cache replication; automatic failover in <60s to meet your SLA.
- Expected cost delta vs current commit: +18% annual (pricing sheet attached).

Next steps: if that option looks acceptable, I’ll loop Legal/Finance to prepare an amendment and schedule a migration runbook session with your infra team next week.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Account Lead, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
From: Claire Brooks <claire@opsly.ai>
To: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Opsly dedicated renewal — hot-standby topology & scale proposal

David — thanks, appreciate the quick read on our telemetry. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The CSV you referenced is what Procurement exported from our observability; it should match. I attached a separate slice showing model-mix per week (we currently run small LLMs for search + a spike of large LLM inference for summarization).
- Our tolerance for cost increase is capped at ~20% year-over-year for this renewal; the hard constraint is zero downtime for live customers during migration.

Questions:
1) What does the hot-standby license look like operationally — do we pay full commit for those slots or a reduced standby rate?
2) Can we start with a lighter hot-standby (50 slots) and autoscale to 100 if utilization trends up over 8 weeks?

Procurement is cc'd — they'll want the pricing breakouts and any contract language that defines failover testing windows.

-Claire
VP Product, Opsly

Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Opsly dedicated renewal — hot-standby topology & scale proposal

Team — forwarding Opsly's clarifying questions. High level asks: 1) confirm hot-standby billing model and a staged scale plan (50 -> 100), 2) ensure failover <60s with prefix/KV replication, 3) final price remains within ~20% delta.

Karthik — can you propose a short SLA amendment language (failover test windows and paid standby terms) and a staged autoscale policy we can show Claire?
Marissa — put together the SKU pricing breakout (annualized) and an 8-week cadence plan for performance checks during staged ramp.
Connor — please include a short runbook blurb for a non-disruptive migration (including canary traffic percentages and step-down rollback).

I'll consolidate and share a single PDF for Opsly by tomorrow EOD.

-David

Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Opsly dedicated renewal — hot-standby topology & scale proposal

David / team / Claire — draft replies inline below.

1) Hot-standby billing model: we can offer a reduced standby rate at 40% of full-commit list for the warm slots (license + reserved hardware). That covers kernel warmup and cache residency. Billing will be monthly; we can codify a 30-day notice to switch standby to active without penalty.

2) Staged scale plan: agree to 50 -> 100 hot-standby ramp over an 8-week observation window. Autoscaling will be governed by a utilization trigger: when steady-state H100-equivalent utilization hits 78% for a 72-hour rolling window, the standby pool expands by increments of 25 slots (manual approval required for >100).

3) Failover and replication: engineering confirms prefix/KV replicate to the AZ-standby with expected warmup <45s on the canonical workloads. We'll include a formal failover test in the runbook with rollback markers and SLA test windows.

Attached: redwood-sku-pricing-opsly.xlsx (breakout) and a short topology diagram. Marissa — I left a couple of configuration notes (fanout/burst thresholds) — please confirm numbers before we finalize.

-Karthik

From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Claire Brooks <claire@opsly.ai>, Procurement <procurement@opsly.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 24 Jun 2028 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Opsly dedicated renewal — formal amendment draft and migration runbook (attachments)

Claire / Procurement — attaching the consolidated proposal and amendment draft. Highlights:
- Topology: 360 dedicated H100-equivalent slots + 160 burst A100 slots + 50 hot-standby (option to scale to 100 under staged policy).
- Standby billing: 40% of listed commit per standby slot; conversion notice 30 days.
- SLA failover: automatic failover target <60s; quarterly failover test window with agreed test plan.
- Cost impact: +17.8% annualized vs current commit (spread across committed SKU and standby discount). See redwood-sku-pricing-opsly.xlsx for line-item math.
- Migration runbook (summary): 1) baseline snapshot and staged canary (5% traffic) 2) incremental ramp to 25%, 50%, 100% over 3 business days with perf gates 3) rollback to original pool via weighted routing if P99 > 500ms.

If Procurement is comfortable, please send a statement-of-work acceptance and I’ll have Legal prepare a short amendment and updated order form. We can also schedule a 60-minute runbook review next Tue (your morning).

Thanks — excited to keep Opsly online during the migration and give you more headroom for the model rollout.

-David
David Kim
Account Lead, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-proposed-topology-opsly.pdf (diagram), opsly_usage_q1q2_2028.csv (usage slice), redwood-sku-pricing-opsly.xlsx (pricing breakout)
